name: Source Inspector
description:
Interface for inspecting binding source artifacts before an OpenBindings interface exists. A source inspector reports its supported kinds and discovers bindable targets that tooling can offer to users.

Carried-values rule: sources and bindings are read under the OpenBindings 0.2 line named by this contract. A source may carry only kind, content, description and x- members. A binding may carry only operation, source, content, idempotent, preference, description, deprecated and x- members, each core member with its core type. The implementation MUST refuse a call carrying any other member or a core member of the wrong type before doing its work. Open carrier schemas preserve extensions; their openness does not waive this rule. Binding operation/source members are forwarded verbatim; this interface neither interprets them nor forbids a kind from reading them. Other binding metadata is information, not an instruction. Kinds are best served identifying targets through content.

For a kind answered false, inspectSource refuses before work. For a kind answered true, admitted targets the implementation cannot establish or represent are omitted with exhaustive: false and a limitation; inability to read the source at all refuses the call.

SupportedKind.description: A kind supported for the work this interface performs.

kind.description: Exact, opaque kind as carried by a source.

Source.description: A source as an OpenBindings 0.2 document carries it: an exact kind and optional content read under that kind. Absent content and present JSON null are distinct. Only core source fields and x- extensions may appear; the carried-values rule requires refusal of other members before work.

kind.description: The source's kind, compared by exact equality.

content.description: Content read under the source's kind: any JSON value, absent when the source has none.

Operation.description: Potential OpenBindings operation framing for a bindable target.

BindableTarget.description: A target the source's kind admits, with binding data and optional sound operation framing. The producer MUST omit operation and source from binding, and MUST NOT include a binding member that is neither a core binding field nor x- prefixed. Consumers MUST reject a target violating either restriction. The author assigns operation and source; author-assigned keys win when constructing the final binding. A producer includes binding.idempotent only where the observed source states it.

sourceRef.description: Stable identifier for this target within the source. An implementation offering both inspection and synthesis uses the same identifier for the same target-scope unit. Cross-producer equality is promised only where the kind defines it.

SourceInspection.description: Inventory of targets the kind admits. Excluded targets are not listed; an admitted target the implementation cannot establish or represent makes the result non-exhaustive with a limitation. If the source cannot be read at all, refuse the call.

exhaustive.description: True when targets is the complete list of targets admitted by the source's kind. False means more admitted targets may exist and requires limitation evidence.

InspectionLimitation.description: Machine-readable evidence explaining why a source inspection is not exhaustive.

message.description: Human-readable explanation of what may be missing and why.

details.description: Optional implementation- or kind-specific structured evidence.

KindSupportVerdict.description: Authoritative support verdict for one exact kind. Future optional fields may annotate the verdict but never qualify or soften supported.

kind.description: The exact kind supplied by the caller.

supported.description: True warrants that this implementation knows how to read sources of this exact kind, and their bindings, for its job and never presents a case it cannot handle as handled: it refuses before work or, where the operation defines disclosure, omits and discloses the case. False means every call on this kind is refused before work.

Binding.description: A binding as an OpenBindings 0.2 document carries it, or would carry it, by value. It is interpreted under the accompanying source's kind. Absent content and present JSON null are distinct. Only core binding fields and x- extensions may appear; the carried-values rule requires refusal of other members before work.

operation.description: The author's operation key, forwarded verbatim without interpretation by this interface.

source.description: The author's source key, forwarded verbatim without interpretation by this interface.

content.description: Content read under the source's kind: any JSON value, absent when the binding has none.

idempotent.description: The binding author's idempotency claim, carried as information.

preference.description: The author's preference signal, carried as information.

deprecated.description: The author's deprecation signal, carried as information.

openbindings.source-inspector.listSuppor.description: Return an advisory list of kinds supported for this interface's job, for display, documentation and pickers. Every listed kind MUST receive supported: true from this interface's checkKindSupport. Absence carries no information and MUST NOT be treated as a negative support decision. This operation is idempotent: repeating it with the same input in context that does not change its intended effects produces no additional intended operation-level effects after the first application. This does not promise identical results or authorize retries.

openbindings.source-inspector.checkKindS.description: Authoritatively determine support for exact kinds for this interface's job. This is the only operation on which a consumer may base a support decision. Return one verdict per unique input kind in first-occurrence order. True warrants that the implementation knows how to read the kind for this job, whether its meaning is written, private or defined only in code. True does not promise every case is within reach; an unhandled case is never presented as handled. False means every call on the kind is refused before work. For a kind answered false, inspectSource refuses before work. For a kind answered true, admitted targets the implementation cannot establish or represent are omitted with exhaustive: false and a limitation; inability to read the source at all refuses the call. The result is deterministic for a given implementation version and configuration. Kinds compare by exact equality: no normalization, case folding, prefix matching, inferred version order or dereferencing. An internal pattern may compress the supported set but MUST NOT extend it. Future optional verdict fields may annotate a verdict but never qualify supported. This operation is idempotent: repeating it with the same input in context that does not change its intended effects produces no additional intended operation-level effects after the first application. This does not promise identical results or authorize retries. The check MUST have no side effects; it neither acquires nor modifies source artifacts or performs the interface job.

openbindings.source-inspector.inspectSou.description: Inspect a binding source artifact and return targets admitted by its source's kind, optionally with sound operation framing. The result states whether enumeration is exhaustive and explains any partial result. This operation is idempotent: repeating it with the same input in context that does not change its intended effects produces no additional intended operation-level effects after the first application. This does not promise identical results or authorize retries. The producer MUST omit operation and source from binding, and MUST NOT include a binding member that is neither a core binding field nor x- prefixed. Consumers MUST reject a target violating either restriction. The author assigns operation and source; author-assigned keys win when constructing the final binding. Operation framing MUST omit idempotent, a binding claim. For composition use {...target.binding, operation: authorOperationKey, source: authorSourceKey}, so author keys win. After substituting a source or binding, the caller owns the edited correspondence claim.
